The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} {{Shrine |name = Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine |location = 1 Ryozen-cho, Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture |coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|0|N|135|46|59|E|display=inline,title}} |deities = 73,011 souls of those who died for the country |rank = Gokoku Shrine designated by the Minister of Home Affairs, Beppyo Shrine |established = 1868 (1st year of Meiji) |annual_festival = April 28, October 14 |image = [[Image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]]
Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[cherry blossoms]] and [[chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement Ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major Festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand Festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama Festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand Festival - October 14 * Ryoma Festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==

拝殿 |地図 = Japan Kyoto city2 |ラベル位置=left }} '''京都霊山護国神社'''（きょうとりょうぜんごこくじんじゃ）は、[[京都市]][[東山区]]清閑寺霊山町にある[[神社]]（[[護国神社]]）。現在は[[神社本庁]]の管理を離れた[[別表神社]]。神紋は[[サクラ|桜]]に[[キク|菊]]。境内の東側は[[明治維新|維新]]の[[志士]]らを祀る[[霊山墓地]]となっている。 == 歴史 == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|「勅を賜り招魂社を建設する事『岩倉公実記』、1906年（明治39年）。国立国会図書館　{{NDLJP|781064/251}}」
（『岩倉公実記』より）]] [[ファイル:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|坂本龍馬・中岡慎太郎像]] [[ファイル:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|陸軍特別操縦見習士官之碑（[[佐藤栄作]]揮毫）]] [[ファイル:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|霊山歴史館]] [[文久]]2年（[[1862年]]）、[[時衆]]霊山派・[[正法寺 (京都市東山区)|正法寺]]の[[朱印地]]の中にある神道葬祭場霊明社朱印地のため買い取りができず、「永世請け持ち」とされ、建前上は時衆葬とされた。において、有志者による殉難者の神葬祭が行われた。祭神は[[菊理媛神]]・[[熊野権現|速玉男命]]・事解男命の3神（他に相殿3神）である。 [[慶応]]4年[[5月10日 (旧暦)|5月10日]]（[[1868年]][[6月29日]]）、[[明治天皇]]から維新を目前にして倒れた[[志士]]たち（[[天誅組]]など）の御霊を奉祀するために、京都・[[東山 (京都府)|東山]]の霊山に佳域社を創建せよとの[[詔]]・御沙汰が発せられた。それに感激した京都の[[公家]]や[[山口藩|山口]]・[[高知藩|高知]]・[[福井藩|福井]]・[[鳥取藩|鳥取]]・[[熊本藩|熊本]]などの諸藩が相計らい、霊山の山頂から山腹にかけてそれぞれの祠宇を建立したのが当社創建のはじまりであり、[[招魂社]]の最初でもあった。[[靖国神社]]よりも一年古い歴史を持つ。 当初の社号は'''霊山官祭招魂社'''と称し、社格にはとくに「官祭社」に列し国費で営繕されてきた。 [[1929年]]（[[昭和]]4年）には、前年に行われた[[昭和天皇]]即位大礼で使用された建物が下賜され、拝殿と斎殿を建立し、いくつもあった祠宇も整備している。 [[1936年]]（昭和11年）、[[日中戦争]]をきっかけとして国難に殉じた京都府出身者の国事殉難者を合祀して手厚く祀ろうという運動がおき、霊山官祭招魂社造営委員会が組織されると、境内を拡大して新たな社殿の造営が行われることとなった。また、維新の志士らを祀る[[霊山墓地]]の整備も行われた。 [[1939年]]（昭和14年）[[4月1日]]、[[内務大臣 (日本)|内務大臣]]布告によって現在の社号である京都霊山護国神社と改称された。また、本殿、拝殿、祝詞舎、神饌所、斎殿などが完成している。 [[太平洋戦争]]に敗北後、当社は国家の手を離れ、[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]に加列されている。 [[連合国軍最高司令官総司令部|GHQ]]占領下においては'''京都神社'''に改称していたが、[[日本国との平和条約|サンフランシスコ講和条約]]後は元の社名に復した。 戦後、霊山墓地は整備されることなく荒れ果ててしまっていたが、それを見かねた松下電器産業（現・[[パナソニックホールディングス]]）会長の[[松下幸之助]]は、[[明治維新]]百年となる[[1968年]]（昭和43年）に自らが中心となって、関西財界人と協力し「霊山顕彰会」を設立。霊山墓地の整備を行い、[[1970年]]（昭和45年）に[[明治維新]]関係の資料を展示する「[[霊山歴史館]]」を開館させた。 [[2002年]]（[[平成]]14年）、神社本庁との包括関係を解消したが、引き続き別表神社である。 祭神の中には京都で暗殺された[[坂本龍馬]]も含まれており、境内に銅像が作られているほか、誕生日であり命日でもある[[11月15日]]には、龍馬の遺徳を偲び霊を慰める龍馬祭が行われる（誕生日・命日は本来は[[11月15日 (旧暦)|旧暦11月15日]]だが、祭は新暦11月15日に行われる）。 [[1997年]]（[[平成]]9年）、[[大東亜戦争]]（太平洋戦争）を記念した「平和記念公園 昭和の杜」が設けられた。 また、[[2012年]]（平成24年）4月には[[特攻勇士の像]]が建立された。 当社の南には龍馬の葬式を行った[[霊明神社]]がある。 == 幻の西郷隆盛像建立計画 == [[1977年]]（昭和52年）の[[西郷隆盛]]没後100年事業として境内に[[西郷隆盛像|西郷像]]を建立する計画が関西在住の[[鹿児島県]]出身者らにより立案され、彫刻家・[[古賀忠雄]]の手により人物立像としては日本最大の10.5メートルに及ぶ西郷像が[[1976年]]（昭和51年）に完成した。しかし、建立の前に依頼者が死去したことにより計画が宙に浮き、この構想は幻となった。 完成した像はそのまま[[富山県]][[高岡市]]の倉庫に保管されていたが、[[1988年]]（昭和63年）に鹿児島県[[姶良郡]][[溝辺町]]（現・[[霧島市]]）へ誘致され、現在は周辺一帯が[[西郷公園]]として整備されている。 == 祭神 == * 国事殉難者7万3千11柱 - [[坂本龍馬]]、[[中岡慎太郎]]、[[木戸孝允]]、[[頼三樹三郎]]、[[梅田雲浜]]、[[吉村虎太郎|吉村寅太郎]]、[[平野国臣]]、[[久坂玄瑞]]、[[高杉晋作]]、[[所郁太郎]]、[[宮部鼎蔵]]、田岡俊三郎ら幕末勤王の志士1,356柱、明治以降の[[日清戦争]]、[[日露戦争]]、[[日中戦争]]、[[太平洋戦争]]などの戦死者を含めた73､011柱が祭神として祀られている。 == 境内 == * 本殿 - [[1939年]]（[[昭和]]14年）4月1日再建。 * 拝殿 - 1939年（昭和14年）4月1日再建。 * 祝詞舎 - 1939年（昭和14年）4月1日建立。 * 神饌所 - 1939年（昭和14年）4月1日建立。 * 斎殿 - 1939年（昭和14年）4月1日再建。 * 社務所 * 東社務所 - 霊山墓地への入口に隣接している。 * [[第116師団 (日本軍)|第百十六師団]]衛生隊顕彰碑 * 嵐第六二二七部隊 [[輜重兵第116連隊|輜重兵第百十六連隊]]顕彰之碑 * 工兵第五十三連隊顕彰碑 * [[歩兵第120連隊|歩兵第百二十連隊]]鎮魂の碑 * 第二十三野戦[[防疫給水部]]戦没者慰霊碑 * [[華北|北支]][[沖縄県|沖縄]]戦没勇士慰霊碑 * [[歩兵第109連隊|歩兵第百九連隊]]顕彰之碑 * 御宸筆歩兵第百九連隊軍旗奉納之地 * 歩兵第百二十八連隊顕彰之碑 * [[特攻勇士の像]] - [[2012年]]（[[平成]]24年）4月造。 * [[霊山歴史館]] - [[1970年]]（昭和45年）に松下幸之助が中心となり設立、開館。道路を挟んで向かい側にある。 === 霊山墓地 === 維新の志士らを祀る霊山墓地は境内の東側の山腹にある。 * [[京都府|京都]]招魂社 * [[山口県|山口]]招魂社 * [[高知県|高知]]招魂社 * [[茨城県|茨城]]招魂社 * [[熊本県|熊本]]招魂社 * [[鳥取県|鳥取]]招魂社 * [[福岡県|福岡]]招魂社 * [[岐阜県|岐阜]]招魂場 * [[坂本龍馬]]・[[中岡慎太郎]]の像 * 陸軍特別操縦見習士官之碑 * [[土佐藩]] ** 坂本龍馬の墓 ** 中岡慎太郎の墓 ** [[吉村虎太郎|吉村寅太郎]]の墓 ** [[望月亀弥太]]の墓 ** [[那須信吾]]の墓 ** [[池内蔵太]]の墓 ** [[天誅組]]の墓 * [[長州藩]] ** [[木戸孝允|桂小五郎 (木戸孝允)]]の墓 ** [[木戸松子|幾松]]の墓 ** [[高杉晋作]]の墓 ** [[久坂玄瑞]]の墓 ** [[大村益次郎]]の墓 ** [[入江九一]]の墓 ** [[寺島忠三郎]]の墓 ** [[来島又兵衛]]の墓 ** [[有吉熊次郎]]の墓 ** [[禁門の変]]戦没者の墓 ** [[池田屋事件]]殉職者の墓 * [[小浜藩]] ** [[梅田雲浜]]の碑 * [[熊本藩]] ** [[河上彦斎]]の墓 ** [[宮部鼎蔵]]の墓 ** [[横井小楠]]の墓 * [[水戸藩]] ** [[江幡広光]]の墓 ** [[林忠五郎]]の墓 ** [[住谷寅之介]]の墓 * [[福岡藩]] ** [[平野国臣]]の墓 * その他 ** [[十津川郷士]]の墓 ** [[山田藤吉]]の墓 == 昭和の杜 == [[1997年]]（[[平成]]9年）、[[大東亜戦争]]（[[太平洋戦争]]）を記念した「平和記念公園 昭和の杜」が設けられた。 * [[ラダ・ビノード・パール|パール博士]]顕彰碑 - [[極東国際軍事裁判]]（東京裁判）にて、ただ一人被告全員の無罪を唱えたインド代表判事。[[インド]]独立50周年を記念して建立された。 == 主な祭典 == * 歳旦祭 - [[1月1日|1月1]]から[[1月3日|3日]] * [[紀元節|紀元祭]] - [[2月11日]] * 春季例大祭 - [[4月28日]] * [[大祓]] * みたま祭 - [[8月13日|8月13]]から[[8月16日|16日]] * 秋季例大祭 - [[10月14日]] * 龍馬祭 - [[11月15日]] * [[天長祭]] - [[12月23日]] == 交通 == * [[京都市営バス]][[京都市営バス梅津営業所#80・特80号系統|80]]・[[京都市営バス九条営業所#202・快速202号系統|202]]・[[京都市営バス烏丸営業所#206号系統|206]]・[[京都市営バス九条営業所#207号系統|207]]系統「東山安井」バス停下車、徒歩10分。 * [[京阪本線]] [[祇園四条駅]]から徒歩15分。 * [[阪急京都本線]][[京都河原町駅]]から徒歩19分。 == その他 == [[2009年]]（平成21年）頃から、[[11月15日]]の坂本龍馬の命日祭の前後に、一部のファンが龍馬の墓に火のついた[[紙巻きたばこ|煙草]]を供えるケースが多発している。2009年（平成21年）の命日祭では、100本以上の煙草が置かれたことで濃い煙が上がり、[[祝詞]]を上げるのに支障が生じた。龍馬が愛煙家だったかは不明だが、舶来の[[銃]]や[[ブーツ]]を所持していたことなどで、外国産の煙草も好んでいたとの考えが広まった可能性がある。同神社の木村隆比古[[宮司]]は「せめて火を付けずに置いてほしい」とコメントしている[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm 龍馬もけむい、墓前に紫煙モクモク…命日に百本] 読売新聞 2010年11月15日。 同神社は日本画家の[[小早川秋聲]]が描いた「戦争画」を所蔵しているが、秋聲の代表作とされる「國の盾」や「御旗」{{Cite web |url=https://www.bunpaku.or.jp/exhi_special_post/kobayakawashusei/ |title=小早川秋聲　旅する画家の鎮魂歌 |access-date=2024-09-27 |publisher=[[京都文化博物館]]}}などの戦争画7点は彼の故郷である[[鳥取県]][[日野町 (鳥取県)|日野町]]の「日野町美術館」に寄託されている{{Cite web |url=http://culture.town.nichinan.tottori.jp/nichinan-museum/category3/entry24.html |title=小早川秋聲展 |access-date=2024-09-27 |publisher=日野町 |website=日野町美術館}}。 == 注釈 ==

[[坂本龍馬]]、[[中岡慎太郎]]、[[木戸孝允]]、[[頼三樹三郎]]、[[梅田雲浜]]、[[吉村虎太郎|吉村寅太郎]]、[[平野国臣]]、[[久坂玄瑞]]、[[高杉晋作]]、[[所郁太郎]]、[[宮部鼎蔵]]、田岡俊三郎ら幕末勤王の志士1,356柱、明治以降の[[日清戦争]]、[[日露戦争]]、[[日中戦争]]、[[太平洋戦争]]などの戦死者を含めた73､011柱が祭神として祀られている。 {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Kyoto, Japan}} [[ja:京都霊山護国神社]] {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} | image = Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg | caption = Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|00|00|N|135|46|59|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = 1868 | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{multiple image| align = right | direction = horizontal | header = | header_align = left/right/center | footer = '''Left image''': Tomb of Sakamoto Ryōma, in ''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine'', [[Kyoto]].
'''Right image''': Tomb of [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] (detail).| footer_align = left | image1 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma torii.jpg| width1 = 137 | caption1 = | image2 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma center.jpg| width2 = 263 | caption2 = }} The {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} is a Shinto Shrine located in [[Kyoto]], [[Japan]]. It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Martin, Phyllis G. Martin p.65] most famously [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] and his associate [[Nakaoka Shintarō]], who are buried side by side in the shrine. Within the shrine is a monument in memory of the [[Bengalis|Bengali]] jurist [[Radhabinod Pal]]. The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} {{Shrine |name = Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine |location = 1 Ryozen-cho, Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture |coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|0|N|135|46|59|E|display=inline,title}} |deities = 73,011 souls of those who died for the country |rank = Gokoku Shrine designated by the Minister of Home Affairs, Beppyo Shrine |established = 1868 (1st year of Meiji) |annual_festival = April 28, October 14 |image = [[Image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]]
Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[cherry blossoms]] and [[chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement Ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major Festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand Festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama Festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand Festival - October 14 * Ryoma Festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==
== See also == * [[Ryozen Cemetery]] * [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} * [http://www.gokoku.or.jp/ Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine Official Website] {{Shinto footer}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto City]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:GokokuTest]] [[Category:History of Higashiyama-ku]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Higashiyama-ku]] ==History== In 1862, a funeral was held by volunteers at the Shinto burial site Reimeisha in the red seal land (朱印地) of the Shohoji (正法寺) temple of the [[:de:Ji-shu]] Ryozan school. There were 3 festival gods [[Kukurihime]], Hayatama-no-Okami, and Susano Otomo.Since it was a red seal land (朱印地), it could not be purchased, and it was a "permanent contractor". On June 29, 1868, in order to worship the spirits of the [[Shishi (organization)|Shishi]] (tenchu-gumi in order to enshrine a holy spirit etc) who fell from [[Emperor Meiji]] on the verge of the [[Meiji Restoration]], a sacred area of a sacred mountain in [[Higashiyama Ward]], Kyoto, a scholarship was issued to build the structure. The shrine was founded at the summit of Kyoto's [[Kuge]] (aristocratic class) and the feudal lords of [[Chōshū Domain|Yamaguchi]], [[Tosa Domain|Kochi]], [[Fukui Domain|Fukui]], [[Tottori Domain|Tottori]], and [[Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto]]. It has an older history than [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. The original name of the company was called Ryozen Kansai Shokyoshasha, and the company name was especially "Kansaisha" which was repaired at national expense. In 1936 (Showa 11), there was a movement to carefully enshrine the national martyrs from [[Kyoto Prefecture]] who perished after the China Incident (支那事変) in the ([[Second Sino-Japanese War]]). The precincts were expanded and a new shrine was built. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the name of the company was changed to the current name of Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by the Declaration of the Ministry of Home Affairs (内務大臣). After [[World War II]], it was placed under the umbrella of a [[religious corporation]] and [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], and left the state. During the [[Occupation of Japan|GHQ occupation]], it was renamed to Kyoto Shrine, but after Japanese independence it was restored to its original name. In 1970 (Showa 45), the [[Ryozen Museum of History]] was opened in the precincts to display materials related to the [[Meiji Restoration]]. In 2002, the comprehensive relationship with the Association of Shinto Shrines was dissolved. [[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. On November 15, in memory of Ryoma's virtues and comforting spirits The Ryoma Festival was held. In addition to Ryoma, [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Shintaro Nakaoka]], Rai Mikisaburo, Umeda Unpin, Torataro Yoshimura, Kuniomi Hirano, [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], Ikutaro Tokoro, Miyabe Teizo, Shunzaburo Taoka (田岡俊三郎) and others, 1,356 pillars of the late [[Edo period]]. A total of about 73,000 pillars are worshiped as religious gods, including those who died during the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Russo-Japanese War]], and the [[World War II]]. Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==Festivals== *Saitan Festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu Festival ([[Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring Festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit Festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn Festival- October 14 *Ryoma Festival- November 15 *Tencho Festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto]][[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]]

It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[cherry blossoms]] and [[chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement Ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major Festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand Festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama Festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand Festival - October 14 * Ryoma Festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==
== See also == * [[Ryozen Cemetery]] * [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} * [http://www.gokoku.or.jp/ Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine Official Website] {{Shinto footer}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto City]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:History of Higashiyama-ku]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Higashiyama-ku]] ==History== In 1862, a funeral was held by volunteers at the Shinto burial site Reimeisha in the red seal land (朱印地) of the Shohoji (正法寺) temple of the [[:de:Ji-shu]] Ryozan school. There were 3 festival gods [[Kukurihime]], Hayatama-no-Okami, and Susano Otomo.Since it was a red seal land (朱印地), it could not be purchased, and it was a "permanent contractor". On June 29, 1868, in order to worship the spirits of the [[Shishi (organization)|Shishi]] (tenchu-gumi in order to enshrine a holy spirit etc) who fell from [[Emperor Meiji]] on the verge of the [[Meiji Restoration]], a sacred area of a sacred mountain in [[Higashiyama Ward]], Kyoto, a scholarship was issued to build the structure. The shrine was founded at the summit of Kyoto's [[Kuge]] (aristocratic class) and the feudal lords of [[Chōshū Domain|Yamaguchi]], [[Tosa Domain|Kochi]], [[Fukui Domain|Fukui]], [[Tottori Domain|Tottori]], and [[Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto]]. It has an older history than [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. The original name of the company was called Ryozen Kansai Shokyoshasha, and the company name was especially "Kansaisha" which was repaired at national expense. In 1936 (Showa 11), there was a movement to carefully enshrine the national martyrs from [[Kyoto Prefecture]] who perished after the China Incident (支那事変) in the ([[Second Sino-Japanese War]]). The precincts were expanded and a new shrine was built. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the name of the company was changed to the current name of Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by the Declaration of the Ministry of Home Affairs (内務大臣). After [[World War II]], it was placed under the umbrella of a [[religious corporation]] and [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], and left the state. During the [[Occupation of Japan|GHQ occupation]], it was renamed to Kyoto Shrine, but after Japanese independence it was restored to its original name. In 1970 (Showa 45), the [[Ryozen Museum of History]] was opened in the precincts to display materials related to the [[Meiji Restoration]]. In 2002, the comprehensive relationship with the Association of Shinto Shrines was dissolved. [[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. On November 15, in memory of Ryoma's virtues and comforting spirits The Ryoma Festival was held. In addition to Ryoma, [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Shintaro Nakaoka]], Rai Mikisaburo, Umeda Unpin, Torataro Yoshimura, Kuniomi Hirano, [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], Ikutaro Tokoro, Miyabe Teizo, Shunzaburo Taoka (田岡俊三郎) and others, 1,356 pillars of the late [[Edo period]]. A total of about 73,000 pillars are worshiped as religious gods, including those who died during the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Russo-Japanese War]], and the [[World War II]]. Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==Festivals== *Saitan Festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu Festival ([[Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring Festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit Festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn Festival- October 14 *Ryoma Festival- November 15 *Tencho Festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto]][[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]]

[[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. '''Right image''': Tomb of [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] (detail).| footer_align = left | image1 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma torii.jpg| width1 = 137 | caption1 = | image2 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma center.jpg| width2 = 263 | caption2 = }} The {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} is a Shinto Shrine located in [[Kyoto]], [[Japan]]. It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Martin, Phyllis G. Martin p.65] most famously [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] and his associate [[Nakaoka Shintarō]], who are buried side by side in the shrine. Within the shrine is a monument in memory of the [[Bengalis|Bengali]] jurist [[Radhabinod Pal]]. The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} {{Shrine |name = Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine |location = 1 Ryozen-cho, Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture |coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|0|N|135|46|59|E|display=inline,title}} |deities = 73,011 souls of those who died for the country |rank = Gokoku Shrine designated by the Minister of Home Affairs, Beppyo Shrine |established = 1868 (1st year of Meiji) |annual_festival = April 28, October 14 |image = [[Image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]]
Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[cherry blossoms]] and [[chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement Ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major Festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand Festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama Festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand Festival - October 14 * Ryoma Festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==

Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[cherry blossoms]] and [[chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement Ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major Festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand Festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama Festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand Festival - October 14 * Ryoma Festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==
== See also == * [[Ryozen Cemetery]] * [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] * [[Kido Takayoshi]] == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} * [http://www.gokoku.or.jp/ Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine Official Website] {{Shinto footer}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto City]] [[Category:Beppyo Shrines]] [[Category:History of Higashiyama-ku]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Higashiyama-ku]] ==History== In 1862, a funeral was held by volunteers at the Shinto burial site Reimeisha in the red seal land (朱印地) of the Shohoji (正法寺) temple of the [[:de:Ji-shu]] Ryozan school. There were 3 festival gods [[Kukurihime]], Hayatama-no-Okami, and Susano Otomo.Since it was a red seal land (朱印地), it could not be purchased, and it was a "permanent contractor". On June 29, 1868, in order to worship the spirits of the [[Shishi (organization)|Shishi]] (tenchu-gumi in order to enshrine a holy spirit etc) who fell from [[Emperor Meiji]] on the verge of the [[Meiji Restoration]], a sacred area of a sacred mountain in [[Higashiyama Ward]], Kyoto, a scholarship was issued to build the structure. The shrine was founded at the summit of Kyoto's [[Kuge]] (aristocratic class) and the feudal lords of [[Chōshū Domain|Yamaguchi]], [[Tosa Domain|Kochi]], [[Fukui Domain|Fukui]], [[Tottori Domain|Tottori]], and [[Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto]]. It has an older history than [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. The original name of the company was called Ryozen Kansai Shokyoshasha, and the company name was especially "Kansaisha" which was repaired at national expense. In 1936 (Showa 11), there was a movement to carefully enshrine the national martyrs from [[Kyoto Prefecture]] who perished after the China Incident (支那事変) in the ([[Second Sino-Japanese War]]). The precincts were expanded and a new shrine was built. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the name of the company was changed to the current name of Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by the Declaration of the Ministry of Home Affairs (内務大臣). After [[World War II]], it was placed under the umbrella of a [[religious corporation]] and [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], and left the state. During the [[Occupation of Japan|GHQ occupation]], it was renamed to Kyoto Shrine, but after Japanese independence it was restored to its original name. In 1970 (Showa 45), the [[Ryozen Museum of History]] was opened in the precincts to display materials related to the [[Meiji Restoration]]. In 2002, the comprehensive relationship with the Association of Shinto Shrines was dissolved. [[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. On November 15, in memory of Ryoma's virtues and comforting spirits The Ryoma Festival was held. In addition to Ryoma, [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Shintaro Nakaoka]], Rai Mikisaburo, Umeda Unpin, Torataro Yoshimura, Kuniomi Hirano, [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], Ikutaro Tokoro, Miyabe Teizo, Shunzaburo Taoka (田岡俊三郎) and others, 1,356 pillars of the late [[Edo period]]. A total of about 73,000 pillars are worshiped as religious gods, including those who died during the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Russo-Japanese War]], and the [[World War II]]. Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==Festivals== *Saitan Festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu Festival ([[Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring Festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit Festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn Festival- October 14 *Ryoma Festival- November 15 *Tencho Festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]]{{Gokoku Shrines}}[[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:pages from wikipedia]][[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]][[Category:Shinto]] [[Category:Pages from wikipedia]] [[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]]

'''Right image''': Tomb of [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] (detail).| footer_align = left | image1 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma torii.jpg| width1 = 137 | caption1 = | image2 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma center.jpg| width2 = 263 | caption2 = }} The {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} is a Shinto Shrine located in [[Kyoto]], [[Japan]]. It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Martin, Phyllis G. Martin p.65] most famously [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] and his associate [[Nakaoka Shintarō]], who are buried side by side in the shrine. Within the shrine is a monument in memory of the [[Bengalis|Bengali]] jurist [[Radhabinod Pal]]. The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} {{Shrine |name = Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine |location = 1 Ryozen-cho, Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture |coordinates = {{Coord|35|0|0|N|135|46|59|E|display=inline,title}} |deities = 73,011 souls of those who died for the country |rank = Gokoku Shrine designated by the Minister of Home Affairs, Beppyo Shrine |established = 1868 (1st year of Meiji) |annual_festival = April 28, October 14 |image = [[Image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]]
Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[cherry blossoms]] and [[chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement Ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major Festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand Festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama Festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand Festival - October 14 * Ryoma Festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==
