Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} {{multiple image| align = right | direction = horizontal | header = | header_align = left/right/center | footer = '''Left image''': Tomb of Sakamoto Ryōma, in ''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine'', [[Kyoto]].
'''Right image''': Tomb of [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] (detail).| footer_align = left | image1 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma torii.jpg| width1 = 137 | caption1 = | image2 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma center.jpg| width2 = 263 | caption2 = }} The {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} is a Shinto Shrine located in [[Kyoto]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Martin, Phyllis G. Martin p.65] most famously [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] and his associate [[Nakaoka Shintarō]], who are buried side by side in the shrine. Within the shrine is a monument in memory of the [[:en:Bengalis|Bengali]] jurist [[Radhabinod Pal]]. The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[:en:Cherry blossoms|Cherry blossoms]] and [[:en:Chrysanthemums|Chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[:en:Eisaku Sato|Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[:en:General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[:en:Konosuke Matsushita|Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[:en:Panasonic|Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[:en:Choshu Domain|Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kido Matsuko|Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[:en:Ikedaya Incident|Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[:en:Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kawakami Gensai|Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[:en:Mito Domain|Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand festival - October 14 * Ryoma festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[:en:Hankyu Kyoto Main Line|Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==
== See also == * [[Ryozen Cemetery]] * [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} * [http://www.gokoku.or.jp/ Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine Official Website] {{Shinto footer}} ==History== In 1862, a funeral was held by volunteers at the Shinto burial site Reimeisha in the red seal land (朱印地) of the Shohoji (正法寺) temple of the [[:de:Ji-shu]] Ryozan school. There were 3 festival gods [[Kukurihime]], Hayatama-no-Okami, and Susano Otomo.Since it was a red seal land (朱印地), it could not be purchased, and it was a "permanent contractor". On June 29, 1868, in order to worship the spirits of the [[Shishi (organization)|Shishi]] (tenchu-gumi in order to enshrine a holy spirit etc) who fell from [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Emperor Meiji]] on the verge of the [[Meiji Restoration]], a sacred area of a sacred mountain in [[:en:Higashiyama Ward|Higashiyama Ward]], Kyoto, a scholarship was issued to build the structure. The shrine was founded at the summit of Kyoto's [[Kuge]] (aristocratic class) and the feudal lords of [[:en:Chōshū Domain|Yamaguchi]], [[Tosa Domain|Kochi]], [[:en:Fukui Domain|Fukui]], [[Tottori Domain|Tottori]], and [[:en:Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto]]. It has an older history than [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. The original name of the company was called Ryozen Kansai Shokyoshasha, and the company name was especially "Kansaisha" which was repaired at national expense. In 1936 (Showa 11), there was a movement to carefully enshrine the national martyrs from [[Kyoto Prefecture]] who perished after the China Incident (支那事変) in the ([[Second Sino-Japanese War]]). The precincts were expanded and a new shrine was built. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the name of the company was changed to the current name of Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by the Declaration of the Ministry of Home Affairs (内務大臣). After [[World War II]], it was placed under the umbrella of a [[religious corporation]] and [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], and left the state. During the [[Occupation of Japan|GHQ occupation]], it was renamed to Kyoto Shrine, but after Japanese independence it was restored to its original name. In 1970 (Showa 45), the [[Ryozen Museum of History]] was opened in the precincts to display materials related to the [[Meiji Restoration]]. In 2002, the comprehensive relationship with the Association of Shinto Shrines was dissolved. [[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. On November 15, in memory of Ryoma's virtues and comforting spirits The Ryoma festival was held. In addition to Ryoma, [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Shintaro Nakaoka]], Rai Mikisaburo, Umeda Unpin, Torataro Yoshimura, Kuniomi Hirano, [[Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], Ikutaro Tokoro, Miyabe Teizo, Shunzaburo Taoka (田岡俊三郎) and others, 1,356 pillars of the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. A total of about 73,000 pillars are worshiped as religious gods, including those who died during the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Russo-Japanese War]], and the [[World War II]]. Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[:en:Kamikaze|Kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==festivals== *Saitan festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu festival ([[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn festival- October 14 *Ryoma festival- November 15 *Tencho festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[:en:India|India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[:en:Gion-Shijō Station|Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Gokoku Shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ \ {{translated page|ja|京都霊山護国神社|version=102590627|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] }} [[image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]] [[sn:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[ja:京都霊山護国神社]] [[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[Category:Buildings in Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. There were 3 festival gods [[Kukurihime]], Hayatama-no-Okami, and Susano Otomo.Since it was a red seal land (朱印地), it could not be purchased, and it was a "permanent contractor". On June 29, 1868, in order to worship the spirits of the [[Shishi (organization)|Shishi]] (tenchu-gumi in order to enshrine a holy spirit etc) who fell from [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Emperor Meiji]] on the verge of the [[Meiji Restoration]], a sacred area of a sacred mountain in [[:en:Higashiyama Ward|Higashiyama Ward]], Kyoto, a scholarship was issued to build the structure. The shrine was founded at the summit of Kyoto's [[Kuge]] (aristocratic class) and the feudal lords of [[:en:Chōshū Domain|Yamaguchi]], [[Tosa Domain|Kochi]], [[:en:Fukui Domain|Fukui]], [[Tottori Domain|Tottori]], and [[:en:Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto]]. It has an older history than [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. The original name of the company was called Ryozen Kansai Shokyoshasha, and the company name was especially "Kansaisha" which was repaired at national expense. In 1936 (Showa 11), there was a movement to carefully enshrine the national martyrs from [[Kyoto Prefecture]] who perished after the China Incident (支那事変) in the ([[Second Sino-Japanese War]]). The precincts were expanded and a new shrine was built. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the name of the company was changed to the current name of Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by the Declaration of the Ministry of Home Affairs (内務大臣). After [[World War II]], it was placed under the umbrella of a [[religious corporation]] and [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], and left the state. During the [[Occupation of Japan|GHQ occupation]], it was renamed to Kyoto Shrine, but after Japanese independence it was restored to its original name. In 1970 (Showa 45), the [[Ryozen Museum of History]] was opened in the precincts to display materials related to the [[Meiji Restoration]]. In 2002, the comprehensive relationship with the Association of Shinto Shrines was dissolved. [[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. On November 15, in memory of Ryoma's virtues and comforting spirits The Ryoma festival was held. In addition to Ryoma, [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Shintaro Nakaoka]], Rai Mikisaburo, Umeda Unpin, Torataro Yoshimura, Kuniomi Hirano, [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], Ikutaro Tokoro, Miyabe Teizo, Shunzaburo Taoka (田岡俊三郎) and others, 1,356 pillars of the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. A total of about 73,000 pillars are worshiped as religious gods, including those who died during the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Russo-Japanese War]], and the [[World War II]]. Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[:en:Kamikaze|Kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==festivals== *Saitan festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu festival ([[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn festival- October 14 *Ryoma festival- November 15 *Tencho festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[:en:India|India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[:en:Gion-Shijō Station|Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Gokoku Shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ \ {{translated page|ja|京都霊山護国神社|version=102590627|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] }} [[image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]] [[sn:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[ja:京都霊山護国神社]] [[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[Category:Buildings in Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} {{multiple image| align = right | direction = horizontal | header = | header_align = left/right/center | footer = '''Left image''': Tomb of Sakamoto Ryōma, in ''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine'', [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]].
'''Right image''': Tomb of [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] (detail).| footer_align = left | image1 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma torii.jpg| width1 = 137 | caption1 = | image2 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma center.jpg| width2 = 263 | caption2 = }} The {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} is a Shinto Shrine located in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Martin, Phyllis G. Martin p.65] most famously [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] and his associate [[Nakaoka Shintarō]], who are buried side by side in the shrine. Within the shrine is a monument in memory of the [[:en:Bengalis|Bengali]] jurist [[Radhabinod Pal]]. The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[:en:Cherry blossoms|Cherry blossoms]] and [[:en:Chrysanthemums|Chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[:en:Eisaku Sato|Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[:en:General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[:en:Konosuke Matsushita|Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[:en:Panasonic|Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[:en:India|India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[:en:Gion-Shijō Station|Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Gokoku Shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ \ {{translated page|ja|京都霊山護国神社|version=102590627|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] }} [[image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]] [[sn:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[ja:京都霊山護国神社]] [[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[Category:Buildings in Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} {{multiple image| align = right | direction = horizontal | header = | header_align = left/right/center | footer = '''Left image''': Tomb of Sakamoto Ryōma, in ''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine'', [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]].
'''Right image''': Tomb of [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] (detail).| footer_align = left | image1 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma torii.jpg| width1 = 137 | caption1 = | image2 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma center.jpg| width2 = 263 | caption2 = }} The {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} is a Shinto Shrine located in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Martin, Phyllis G. Martin p.65] most famously [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] and his associate [[Nakaoka Shintarō]], who are buried side by side in the shrine. Within the shrine is a monument in memory of the [[:en:Bengalis|Bengali]] jurist [[Radhabinod Pal]]. The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[:en:Kyoto City|Kyoto City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[:en:Cherry blossoms|Cherry blossoms]] and [[:en:Chrysanthemums|Chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[:en:Eisaku Sato|Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[:en:General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[:en:Konosuke Matsushita|Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[:en:Panasonic|Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[:en:Choshu Domain|Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kido Matsuko|Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[:en:Ikedaya Incident|Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[:en:Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kawakami Gensai|Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[:en:Mito Domain|Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - the Indian judge who advocated for the innocence of all defendants at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] (Tokyo Trials). Erected in commemoration of the 50th anniversary of India's independence. == Major festivals == * Saitansai - January 1 to January 3 * Kigensai - February 11 * Spring Grand festival - April 28 * Oharae - June 30 and December 31 * Mitama festival - August 13 to August 16 * Autumn Grand festival - October 14 * Ryoma festival - November 15 * Tenchosai - December 23 == Access == * 10 minutes on foot from "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop on Kyoto City Bus lines 80, 202, 206, and 207. * 15 minutes on foot from [[Gion Shijo Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. * 19 minutes on foot from [[Kyoto Kawaramachi Station]] on the [[:en:Hankyu Kyoto Main Line|Hankyu Kyoto Main Line]]. == Others == Since around 2009 (Heisei 21), some fans have been offering lit cigarettes at Sakamoto Ryoma's grave around his memorial festival on November 15. In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==
== See also == * [[Ryozen Cemetery]] * [[Sakamoto Ryoma]] * [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] == External Links == {{Commonscat|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} * [http://www.gokoku.or.jp/ Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine Official Website] {{Shinto footer}} ==History== In 1862, a funeral was held by volunteers at the Shinto burial site Reimeisha in the red seal land (朱印地) of the Shohoji (正法寺) temple of the [[:de:Ji-shu]] Ryozan school. There were 3 festival gods [[Kukurihime]], Hayatama-no-Okami, and Susano Otomo.Since it was a red seal land (朱印地), it could not be purchased, and it was a "permanent contractor". On June 29, 1868, in order to worship the spirits of the [[Shishi (organization)|Shishi]] (tenchu-gumi in order to enshrine a holy spirit etc) who fell from [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Emperor Meiji]] on the verge of the [[Meiji Restoration]], a sacred area of a sacred mountain in [[:en:Higashiyama Ward|Higashiyama Ward]], Kyoto, a scholarship was issued to build the structure. The shrine was founded at the summit of Kyoto's [[Kuge]] (aristocratic class) and the feudal lords of [[:en:Chōshū Domain|Yamaguchi]], [[Tosa Domain|Kochi]], [[:en:Fukui Domain|Fukui]], [[Tottori Domain|Tottori]], and [[:en:Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto]]. It has an older history than [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. The original name of the company was called Ryozen Kansai Shokyoshasha, and the company name was especially "Kansaisha" which was repaired at national expense. In 1936 (Showa 11), there was a movement to carefully enshrine the national martyrs from [[Kyoto Prefecture]] who perished after the China Incident (支那事変) in the ([[Second Sino-Japanese War]]). The precincts were expanded and a new shrine was built. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the name of the company was changed to the current name of Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by the Declaration of the Ministry of Home Affairs (内務大臣). After [[World War II]], it was placed under the umbrella of a [[religious corporation]] and [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], and left the state. During the [[Occupation of Japan|GHQ occupation]], it was renamed to Kyoto Shrine, but after Japanese independence it was restored to its original name. In 1970 (Showa 45), the [[Ryozen Museum of History]] was opened in the precincts to display materials related to the [[Meiji Restoration]]. In 2002, the comprehensive relationship with the Association of Shinto Shrines was dissolved. [[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. On November 15, in memory of Ryoma's virtues and comforting spirits The Ryoma festival was held. In addition to Ryoma, [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Shintaro Nakaoka]], Rai Mikisaburo, Umeda Unpin, Torataro Yoshimura, Kuniomi Hirano, [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], Ikutaro Tokoro, Miyabe Teizo, Shunzaburo Taoka (田岡俊三郎) and others, 1,356 pillars of the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. A total of about 73,000 pillars are worshiped as religious gods, including those who died during the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Russo-Japanese War]], and the [[World War II]]. Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[:en:Kamikaze|Kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==festivals== *Saitan festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu festival ([[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn festival- October 14 *Ryoma festival- November 15 *Tencho festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[:en:India|India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[:en:Gion-Shijō Station|Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Gokoku Shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ \ {{translated page|ja|京都霊山護国神社|version=102590627|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] }} [[image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]] [[sn:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[ja:京都霊山護国神社]] [[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[Category:Buildings in Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Haiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Norito-sha - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shinzenjo - built on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Saiden - rebuilt on April 1, 1939 (Showa 14) * Shrine office * Eastern shrine office - adjacent to the entrance of Ryozen Cemetery * 116th Division Memorial Monument * 6227th Unit Memorial Monument * 53rd Engineer Regiment Memorial Monument * 120th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * 23rd Field Hygiene and Water Supply Unit Memorial Monument * Memorial Monument for War Dead from North China and Okinawa * 109th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Monument for the Dedication of the Military Flag of the 109th Infantry Regiment * 128th Infantry Regiment Memorial Monument * Statue of the Kamikaze Warriors - erected in April 2012 (Heisei 24) * Ryozen Historical Museum - established by Konosuke Matsushita and opened in 1970 (Showa 45), located across the street === Ryozen Cemetery === The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines Meiji Restoration loyalists, is located on the eastern hillside of the shrine grounds. * Kyoto Shokonsha * Yamaguchi Shokonsha * Kochi Shokonsha * Ibaraki Shokonsha * Kumamoto Shokonsha * Tottori Shokonsha * Fukuoka Shokonsha * Gifu Shokonjo * Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro * Memorial Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers * [[Tosa Domain]] ** Grave of Sakamoto Ryoma ** Grave of Nakaoka Shintaro ** Grave of [[Yoshimura Torataro]] ** Grave of [[Mochizuki Kameyata]] ** Grave of [[Nasu Shingo]] ** Grave of [[Ike Kurato]] ** Grave of the [[Tenchu-gumi]] * [[:en:Choshu Domain|Choshu Domain]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kido Matsuko|Kido Matsuko]] ** Grave of [[Takasugi Shinsaku]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]] ** Grave of [[Omura Masujiro]] ** Grave of [[Irie Kuichi]] ** Grave of [[Terajima Tanzaemon]] ** Grave of [[Raikou Motosuke]] ** Grave of the war dead of the [[Forbidden Gate Incident]] ** Grave of those who died in the [[:en:Ikedaya Incident|Ikedaya Incident]] * [[Obama Domain]] ** Monument of [[Umeda Unpin]] * [[:en:Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto Domain]] ** Grave of [[:en:Kawakami Gensai|Kawakami Gensai]] ** Grave of [[Miyabe Teizo]] ** Grave of [[Yokoi Shonan]] * [[:en:Mito Domain|Mito Domain]] ** Grave of [[Enba Hirokage]] ** Grave of [[Hayashi Tadagoro]] ** Grave of [[Sumitani Toranosuke]] * [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]] ** Grave of [[Hirano Kuniomi]] * Others ** Grave of [[Totsukawa-goshi]] ** Grave of [[Yamada Fujio]] == Showa no Mori == In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. * Memorial Monument of Judge [[Radhabinod Pal]] - In 2009 (Heisei 21), over 100 cigarettes were placed, causing thick smoke and disrupting the prayer rituals. Although it is unclear if Ryoma was a smoker, there is speculation that he liked foreign cigarettes due to his possession of imported guns and boots. Shrine priest Takahiko Kimura has commented, "Please at least refrain from lighting them."[http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/national/news/20101115-OYT1T00574.htm "Ryoma too smoky, over 100 cigarettes offered at grave on memorial day"] Yomiuri Shimbun, November 15, 2010. == Notes ==

There were 3 festival gods [[Kukurihime]], Hayatama-no-Okami, and Susano Otomo.Since it was a red seal land (朱印地), it could not be purchased, and it was a "permanent contractor". On June 29, 1868, in order to worship the spirits of the [[Shishi (organization)|Shishi]] (tenchu-gumi in order to enshrine a holy spirit etc) who fell from [[:en:Emperor Meiji|Emperor Meiji]] on the verge of the [[Meiji Restoration]], a sacred area of a sacred mountain in [[:en:Higashiyama Ward|Higashiyama Ward]], Kyoto, a scholarship was issued to build the structure. The shrine was founded at the summit of Kyoto's [[Kuge]] (aristocratic class) and the feudal lords of [[:en:Chōshū Domain|Yamaguchi]], [[Tosa Domain|Kochi]], [[:en:Fukui Domain|Fukui]], [[Tottori Domain|Tottori]], and [[:en:Kumamoto Domain|Kumamoto]]. It has an older history than [[Yasukuni Shrine]]. The original name of the company was called Ryozen Kansai Shokyoshasha, and the company name was especially "Kansaisha" which was repaired at national expense. In 1936 (Showa 11), there was a movement to carefully enshrine the national martyrs from [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]] who perished after the China Incident (支那事変) in the ([[Second Sino-Japanese War]]). The precincts were expanded and a new shrine was built. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the name of the company was changed to the current name of Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by the Declaration of the Ministry of Home Affairs (内務大臣). After [[World War II]], it was placed under the umbrella of a [[religious corporation]] and [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], and left the state. During the [[Occupation of Japan|GHQ occupation]], it was renamed to Kyoto Shrine, but after Japanese independence it was restored to its original name. In 1970 (Showa 45), the [[Ryozen Museum of History]] was opened in the precincts to display materials related to the [[Meiji Restoration]]. In 2002, the comprehensive relationship with the Association of Shinto Shrines was dissolved. [[Ryoma Sakamoto]], who was assassinated in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], is also included in the deity, and a statue was built in the precincts. On November 15, in memory of Ryoma's virtues and comforting spirits The Ryoma festival was held. In addition to Ryoma, [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Shintaro Nakaoka]], Rai Mikisaburo, Umeda Unpin, Torataro Yoshimura, Kuniomi Hirano, [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], Ikutaro Tokoro, Miyabe Teizo, Shunzaburo Taoka (田岡俊三郎) and others, 1,356 pillars of the late [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]]. A total of about 73,000 pillars are worshiped as religious gods, including those who died during the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], the [[Russo-Japanese War]], and the [[World War II]]. Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[:en:Kamikaze|Kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==festivals== *Saitan festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu festival ([[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn festival- October 14 *Ryoma festival- November 15 *Tencho festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[:en:India|India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[:en:Gion-Shijō Station|Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Gokoku Shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ \ {{translated page|ja|京都霊山護国神社|version=102590627|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] }} [[image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]] [[sn:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[ja:京都霊山護国神社]] [[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[Category:Buildings in Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]

Haiden |map = Japan Kyoto city2 |label_position=left }} {{multiple image| align = right | direction = horizontal | header = | header_align = left/right/center | footer = '''Left image''': Tomb of Sakamoto Ryōma, in ''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine'', [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]].
'''Right image''': Tomb of [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] (detail).| footer_align = left | image1 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma torii.jpg| width1 = 137 | caption1 = | image2 =Tomb of Sakamoto Ryoma center.jpg| width2 = 263 | caption2 = }} The {{nihongo|'''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' | 京都霊山護国神社|Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku Jinja}} is a Shinto Shrine located in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It honors the heroes of Japan, especially from the period of the [[:en:Bakumatsu|Bakumatsu]] period and the [[Meiji Restoration]],[https://books.google.com/books?id=YRCWtf_d5jgC&pg=PA65 ''Kyoto Cultural Guide'' by John H. Martin, Phyllis G. Martin p.65] most famously [[Sakamoto Ryōma]] and his associate [[Nakaoka Shintarō]], who are buried side by side in the shrine. Within the shrine is a monument in memory of the [[:en:Bengalis|Bengali]] jurist [[Radhabinod Pal]]. The [[Ryozen Museum of History]] is next to this shrine. ==Overview== {{cite sources|date=August 28, 2017}} '''Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine''' (京都霊山護国神社, Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Jinja) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Seikanji, Higashiyama-ku, [[:en:Kyoto City|Kyoto City]], [[:en:Kyoto Prefecture|Kyoto Prefecture]]. Currently, it is a Beppyo Shrine not under the administration of the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The shrine emblem (kamon) features [[:en:Cherry blossoms|Cherry blossoms]] and [[:en:Chrysanthemums|Chrysanthemums]]. The eastern part of the shrine grounds is the Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrines the souls of [[Meiji Restoration]] loyalists. == History == [[File:招魂社岩倉.jpg|thumb|250px|An imperial decree to establish the Shokonsha shrine'Iwakura Ko Jikki', 1906 (Meiji 39). National Diet Library {{NDLJP|781064/251}}]] [[File:Reizan6420.jpg|thumb|250px|Statues of Sakamoto Ryoma and Nakaoka Shintaro]] [[File:Reizan6317.jpg|thumb|250px|Monument for Special Flight Trainee Officers (inscribed by [[:en:Eisaku Sato|Eisaku Sato]])]] [[File:Ryozen Museum of History01-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Ryozen Historical Museum]] In 1862 (Bunkyu 2), a Shinto funeral was held for the martyrs at the Shinto burial ground Reimei-sha in the precincts of Shohoji, a temple of the Jishu Ryozen sect.As the land was under the control of the temple, the funeral was formally a Jishu funeral. The deities enshrined were Kukunochi-no-Mikoto, Hayatama-no-Mikoto, and Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto (with three other deities enshrined together). On May 10, 1868 (Keio 4), an imperial decree by Emperor Meiji was issued to create a shrine on Ryozen in eastern Kyoto to enshrine the souls of those who died in the Meiji Restoration efforts, such as the [[Tenchu-gumi]]. This became the origin of the shrine, which was the first Shokonsha shrine, preceding even [[Yasukuni Shrine]] by a year. The original name of the shrine was Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha, and it was classified as an "official shrine" and maintained with national funds. In 1929 (Showa 4), buildings used in the Enthronement ceremony of Emperor Showa were donated, and the Haiden and Saiden were constructed, consolidating the various smaller shrines on the grounds. In 1936 (Showa 11), following the start of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], a movement arose to enshrine and honor those from Kyoto Prefecture who died in national service. The Ryozen Kansai Shokonsha construction committee was formed, leading to the expansion of the grounds and the construction of new shrine buildings. The Ryozen Cemetery, which enshrined Meiji Restoration loyalists, was also improved. On April 1, 1939 (Showa 14), the shrine was renamed Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine by a proclamation from the Minister of Home Affairs. New shrine buildings, including the Honden, Haiden, Norito-sha, Shinzenjo, and Saiden, were completed. After the defeat in [[World War II]], the shrine was removed from state control and registered as a Beppyo Shrine under the Association of Shinto Shrines. During the occupation by the [[:en:General Headquarters|GHQ]], the shrine was temporarily renamed Kyoto Shrine, but reverted to its original name after the [[Treaty of San Francisco]]. The Ryozen Cemetery fell into disrepair post-war, but [[:en:Konosuke Matsushita|Konosuke Matsushita]], the president of Matsushita Electric Industrial (now [[:en:Panasonic|Panasonic]]), took the lead in 1968 (Showa 43) to establish the Ryozen Memorial Association with Kansai business leaders. The cemetery was restored, and in 1970 (Showa 45), the Ryozen Historical Museum, which displays materials related to the Meiji Restoration, was opened. In 2002 (Heisei 14), the shrine terminated its affiliation with the Association of Shinto Shrines but continues to be a Beppyo Shrine. Among the deities enshrined are [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], who was assassinated in Kyoto. A statue of Ryoma stands in the grounds, and on November 15, his birth and death anniversary, a festival called Ryoma-sai is held to honor his memory (the festival is held on the Gregorian calendar date, not the lunar calendar date). In 1997 (Heisei 9), the "Peace Memorial Park Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the [[Pacific War]]. In April 2012 (Heisei 24), the statue of the Kamikaze warriors was erected. To the south of the shrine is Reimei Shrine, where Ryoma's funeral was held. == Unfinished Saigo Takamori Statue Plan == In 1977 (Showa 52), a plan to erect a statue of [[Saigo Takamori]] in the shrine grounds for the 100th anniversary of his death was proposed by a group of Kagoshima natives living in Kansai. Sculptor [[Tadao Koga]] created the statue, which at 10.5 meters would have been the largest standing statue in Japan. However, the death of the project sponsor left the plan unfinished. The completed statue was stored in a warehouse in [[Takaoka]], [[Toyama Prefecture]], until it was moved to [[Mizobe Town]], [[Aira District]], Kagoshima Prefecture (now [[Kirishima City]]) in 1988 (Showa 63), where the surrounding area is now developed as [[Saigo Park]]. == Deities == * 73,011 souls of those who died for the country, including [[Sakamoto Ryoma]], [[Nakaoka Shintaro]], [[:en:Kido Takayoshi|Kido Takayoshi]], [[Rai Sanyo]], [[Umeda Unpin]], [[Yoshimura Torataro]], [[Hirano Kuniomi]], [[:en:Kusaka Genzui|Kusaka Genzui]], [[Takasugi Shinsaku]], [[Tokoro Ikutaro]], [[Miyabe Teizo]], and [[Tadaoka Toshinosuke]], along with 1,356 loyalists of the late Edo period and those who died in the [[:en:First Sino-Japanese War|First Sino-Japanese War]], [[Russo-Japanese War]], [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], and [[Pacific War]]. == Grounds == * Honden - Also, in April 2012, a statue of a [[:en:Kamikaze|Kamikaze]] pilot was erected. ==festivals== *Saitan festival (new years festival) - January 1,～ three days *Kigensetsu festival ([[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]]'s ascension to the throne) - February 11 *Spring festival- April 28 *[[Oharae]] (大祓) (purification festival) *Spirit festival - August 13,～16th *Autumn festival- October 14 *Ryoma festival- November 15 *Tencho festival ([[The Emperor's Birthday]]) - December 23 ==Showa Forest== In 1997 ( Heisei 9), "Showa no Mori" was established to commemorate the Great East Asian War ([[Pacific War]]). To commemorate the 50th anniversary of [[:en:India|India]]'s independence, there is a monument dedicated to India's representative judge, [[Radhabinod Pal]], whose dissenting opinion at the [[:en:International Military Tribunal for the Far East|International Military Tribunal for the Far East]] was that the accused were not guilty of war crimes. ==Transportation== *Take the Kyoto City Bus 80, 202, 206, 207 "Higashiyama Yasui" bus stop and walk 10 minutes. *15 minutes walk from [[:en:Gion-Shijō Station|Gion-Shijō Station]] on the [[:en:Keihan Main Line|Keihan Main Line]]. ==See also== * [[List of Shinto shrines in Japan]] ==Notes== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{Official website |http://www.gokoku.or.jp/en/index.html}} {{Gokoku Shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ \ {{translated page|ja|京都霊山護国神社|version=102590627|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto]] [[Category:Gokoku shrines]] [[Category:Culture articles needing translation from Japanese Wikipedia]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] }} [[image:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine01-r.jpg|250px]] [[sn:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[ja:京都霊山護国神社]] [[en:Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine]] [[Category:Buildings in Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] {{Commons category|Kyoto Ryozen Gokoku Shrine}} [[fa:معبد کیوتو ریوزن گوکوکو]] [[fr:Kyōto Ryōzen Gokoku-jinja]] [[Category:translated pages with valid en interwikis]]
